correctness.rationale: Normalize the four nonzero coefficients to unit modulus. At any Fourier zero, the four unit summands have zero sum; because the first and third elementary symmetric sums vanish, their root polynomial is even and the summands split into antipodal pairs. Prime-order invertibility prevents one pairing from occurring at two distinct frequencies. Three zeros would use all three matchings and force -1 to be a p-th root of unity, impossible for odd p. Two zeros force central symmetry of the support by comparing the two expressions for one coefficient ratio, and explicit unit-modulus coefficients realize two zeros on every centrally symmetric support. The zero-zero and one-zero cases are also explicitly realized.

value.rationale: Equal nonzero coefficient magnitudes define a natural phase-only subclass of sparse Fourier signals. The theorem gives a complete all-prime classification at sparsity four, proves that the unrestricted three-zero extremal disappears, and identifies central symmetry of the support as the exact mechanism allowing two zeros. This is structural information rather than a finite computation or a routine parameter increment.
